description: Add a central dispatch-layer --help/-h short-circuit so no command (incl. internal ones like sidecar) runs a side-effect on --help, and document the deterministic flags.

userStories.title: Central --help/-h short-circuit guard at the dispatch layer covering every command
userStories.description: As an operator, I need `cam <any-command> --help` (including internal commands like `sidecar`) to print usage and exit 0 before any command body runs, so that `cam sidecar --help` never boots the long-lived daemon and no command mutates state on a help probe.
acceptanceCriteria: A single --help/-h short-circuit at the dispatch/arg-parse layer of index.ts runs BEFORE the command switch body and prints usage + exits 0 for the requested command, driven by a command-name to help-text registry (not a per-command guard inside each case). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The registry has a help-text entry for every registered command including the internal ones (sidecar, orch-recycle-watch, sidecar-liveness-watch, orch-budget); new help constants are added for internal commands that currently have none. [oracle: bun index.ts sidecar --help > /dev/null; test $? -eq 0]
`cam sidecar --help` prints usage and exits 0 WITHOUT starting the sidecar daemon (returns promptly, does not hang). [oracle: bun index.ts sidecar --help > /dev/null; test $? -eq 0]

A table-driven test in test/ iterates every registered command, invokes the exported main() with ["bun","index.ts",<cmd>,"--help"], and asserts it returns 0 with non-empty usage output and no daemon spawn / no filesystem or state mutation. [oracle: bun test]

The `cam claude` arg-forwarding semantics are preserved: `cam claude --help` prints CLAUDE_HELP, but a `--help` in a non-leading position is still forwarded to the child claude process (the central guard does not over-capture claude's forwarded args). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Primary file: index.ts (the main() switch, lines ~1971-2329; internal commands sidecar/orch-recycle-watch/sidecar-liveness-watch/orch-budget at ~2189-2272 currently have NO --help guard and run their body immediately — that is the live footgun). Add a registry (e.g. Record<string,string>) mapping command name -> its *_HELP constant, and a central short-circuit before the switch. GOTCHA (root cause per issue): the guard MUST intercept before the command body; a per-command guard re-opens the footgun for every new command and is explicitly rejected. GOTCHA (claude): src/commands/claude.ts forwards all args verbatim and only treats a LEADING --help/-h as its own (see claude.ts header comment lines 10-11); do NOT use a blanket tail.includes('--help') for claude or you break forwarding — the table-driven test uses --help as the sole/first arg so it passes either way, but preserve leading-only semantics for claude. New internal-command help constants can be terse (usage line + one-line 'internal command' note) built via renderHelp (src/logging/help.ts). GOTCHA (CAM-217, patterns.md line 520): renderHelp entry-name column silently drops the separator space when HelpEntry.name >= 24 chars; keep names short and eyeball the rendered `bun index.ts <cmd> --help` output, not just the diff. Test convention: test/dispatch.test.ts and test/issue-dispatch.test.ts show the bun:test + injected-fake style; main is exported from index.ts (bottom, `export { main }`). The existing per-command `if (parsed.help)` blocks become unreachable-for-help once the central guard fires; removing them is optional cleanup (Surgical Changes: keep the diff focused on the guard + registry).

userStories.title: List internal commands in cam --help and document the deterministic flags
userStories.description: As an operator, I need `cam --help` to surface internal commands (like `sidecar`) under an explicit Internal section, and each command's --help to document its deterministic flags (`cam issue --file-local`, the `cam journal append` stdin-JSON schema, and `cam issue close`/`abandon`), so the safe deterministic CLI is discoverable.
acceptanceCriteria: `cam --help` lists the internal commands (sidecar, and the other daemon/watcher internals) under an explicit 'Internal' section, marked as internal rather than as user-facing entry points. [oracle: bun index.ts --help | grep -qi 'internal']
The Internal section names sidecar. [oracle: bun index.ts --help | grep -q 'sidecar']
`cam issue --help` documents the deterministic `--file-local` flag (currently absent from ISSUE_HELP). [oracle: bun index.ts issue --help | grep -q -- '--file-local']
`cam issue --help` documents the deterministic `close <id>` and `abandon <id>` subcommands. [oracle: bun index.ts issue --help | grep -q 'close' && bun index.ts issue --help | grep -q 'abandon']
`cam journal --help` documents the `journal append` stdin-JSON schema (the JournalCycleEntry fields read from stdin). [oracle: bun index.ts journal --help | grep -q 'cycleId']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: File: index.ts. Top-level HELP built via renderHelp at ~line 87-123 — add a second section (heading 'Internal') to the `sections` array listing sidecar (+ orch-recycle-watch/sidecar-liveness-watch/orch-budget as appropriate) with a one-line description; these are spawned by `cam run`, not user entry points. ISSUE_HELP is at ~line 307-358: close/abandon are already documented (Arguments section, lines 327-336) — VERIFY and leave intact; add a `--file-local` entry (the commit-to-main filer used by the orchestrator, see parseIssueArgs discriminated union at ~line 787). JOURNAL_HELP at ~line 360-435 already documents the stdin schema in the Behaviour body (step 1: cycleId, title, started, ...) — VERIFY it lists the JournalCycleEntry fields and leave intact. GOTCHA (CAM-217, patterns.md line 520 + CAM-231/CAM-220 history): when appending an entry to an existing *_HELP Options/Arguments array, keep HelpEntry.name < 24 chars or the description concatenates with no space; check the rendered `bun index.ts issue --help` output. Follow the 'extend, do not restructure' convention from the CAM-217 fix. This is doc-only text in help constants; do not change command behavior (issue scope: OUT = adding new deterministic flags — they already exist, only document them).
